lines: Six buttons.
Two AI agents.
One couch.
This is the Gamebrick, a mini retro controller.
Forty-nine millimeters, ten hours of battery, and it fits in your pocket.
Switch it to C mode, pair it over Bluetooth,
and PocketAgentRemote turns it into a remote for Codex and Claude on your Mac.
Your agent is working. You're not at your desk.
When it asks for approval, you don't need a keyboard.
Just press A.
A is Enter, to submit or approve.
Hold A and talk, for voice input.
B is Escape, to cancel or reject.
The D-pad moves through options, and repeats while you hold it.
And B plus A is backspace, for fixing a misheard word.
It knows which app is in front.
In Codex, B plus up jumps to a recent chat, and B plus right finds the chat that needs you.
In Claude, the same buttons move between chats and open the command palette.
Anywhere else, it's just arrows, Enter, and Escape.
B plus left opens the command menu.
New chat, changes, terminal, model, archive.
It never steals focus, and while it's open, the controller belongs to the menu.
For Codex, there's also an experimental four-way dial.
Hold B for the app switcher.
Left and right to pick, A to jump. Command-Tab, from across the room.
In any other app, B plus left reads that app's own menu bar.
In WeChat, next unread chat and search are pinned to the top.
Anything destructive, like quit, delete, or clear, is never listed.
When a press does nothing, a short notice tells you why.
It launches at login, survives sleep, and warns you if permissions are lost.
And with no controller in hand, the same menus live in the menu bar.
PocketAgentRemote.
Your agents, one pocket away.
